topic: Tracking Typhoons in the Philippine Area of Responsibility
key_concepts: PAGASA tracks typhoons that enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility
Typhoon tracking predicts a typhoon’s path every 6 to 12 hours over at least five days
Computer forecast models help predict typhoon motion 5 to 7 days ahead

Typhoons have lower air pressure at the center or eye
The eye has calm conditions and low wind speed
The eyewall has dense clouds, heavy rains, and very high wind speeds
Air pressure within a typhoon increases as distance from the eye increases
Landmasses disrupt the spin of a typhoon while bodies of water strengthen it
